_meta.subject: Irish actor resident in Dublin
_meta.note: Every figure carries its source and effective date. Where a figure could not be confirmed from a primary or near-primary source it is null and explained under 'uncertain'. Irish Equity keeps its current rate cards behind a members' login (https://irishequity.ie/fees/ returns 'You are required to login to view this page'), so the only performer rate schedule publicly readable is the 2021 SPI/Irish Equity Irish Film Agreement.

union.name: Irish Equity
union.parent: SIPTU (Services, Industrial, Professional and Technical Union)

irishFilmAgreement2021.parties: Screen Producers Ireland (SPI) and Irish Equity
irishFilmAgreement2021.duration: Three years from signature, then continuing until amended by mutual written agreement or terminated on 3 months' written notice (clause 1.2). No successor agreement found publicly, so it is presumed still in force by its rollover clause; see 'uncertain'.
irishFilmAgreement2021.structure: A basic performance fee plus a use fee (a percentage of the basic, varying by budget tier) plus 8% holiday pay, plus a share in a net-profits cast pool. It is not a full buyout.

tiers.budget: Global budget of EUR 2.5m and over
Global budget over EUR 1.25m and up to EUR 2.5m
Global budget of EUR 1.25m and under

otherTerms.holidayPay: 8% of the daily or weekly performance fee, excluding use fees
otherTerms.nightWork: Additional 50% of the basic daily fee
otherTerms.secondCallSession: EUR 50 for a session of not more than 5 hours (tests, fittings, stills); no use fee
otherTerms.readThroughsAndRehearsals: Half the artist's negotiated daily performance fee; no use fee
otherTerms.weatherCancellation: Artist receives the negotiated daily performance fee (no use fee)

irishFilmAgreement2021.note: The tier totals in the schedule are rounded to the euro (e.g. tier 3 daily 158 + 79 + 12.64 = 249.64, printed as 250; weekly 998.56 printed as 999).

tvDramaAgreement2016.parties: Screen Producers Ireland and Irish Equity
tvDramaAgreement2016.covers: Performers on TV drama commissioned by Irish broadcasters; the first collective agreement for artists in Irish TV drama. Moved away from full buyout toward profit participation from programme sales after an initial period. Excludes instrumental musicians, crowd, walk-on/background, stunt artists and dancers in those capacities.
tvDramaAgreement2016.note: The announcement publishes no figures; the rate schedule is not public.

rteDramaRates.note: No public RTÉ/Irish Equity drama rate card found.

marketRateCard2020_secondary.effective: 2020 market rate card (not a collective agreement)
marketRateCard2020_secondary.caveat: Secondary source (Focal / ProdValue, Swiss producers' association comparative survey). It describes prevailing market buyout rates on productions, largely inward international work, not an Irish Equity minimum.

theatreRates.note: No publicly readable Irish Equity / Theatre Forum rate card was found; Irish Equity's fees page is members-only. A blank Irish Equity theatre memorandum of agreement (undated) is public and sets structure but no figures: extra performances beyond the normal week at not less than one-sixth of the weekly salary; hourly rate basis of 1/42 of the weekly engagement fee; overtime at twice the hourly rate; management lodges a bond equal to one week's engagement for all artistes.

historicalFigure.context: Irish Times report on an Arts Council pay study: Abbey wages started at the Equity minimum and rose to EUR 792 for seasoned performers; Gate top rate reported at EUR 700; companies such as Rough Magic or Druid between EUR 550 and EUR 650 a week.
historicalFigure.effective: Undated older article (pre-2010 URL format); NOT a current figure

theatreRates.touringNote: UK Theatre states that touring in the Republic of Ireland is now covered by the UK Theatre/Equity Commercial and Subsidised Theatre Agreements, and the UK Theatre/SOLT/Irish Equity Addendum is no longer in use.

audioRates.note: No public Irish Equity radio/audio or RTÉ radio drama rate card was found. Do not substitute the UK Equity/BBC audio rates, which are a different jurisdiction.

typicalCommission.sharedRepresentationExample: One Irish agent charged 15% on her own clients and 21% (split between agents) when sharing a client with a UK or US agent
typicalCommission.deductible: Agent commission is deductible as a cost of earning the fee for Irish tax purposes
typicalCommission.caveat: Secondary sources (a casting platform guide and an accountant's guide). No agency publishes its commission on its site; none of the verified agency sites below discloses a rate.

section481Spend2025.scope: Total spend in Ireland by all film, TV, documentary and animation projects eligible for the Section 481 incentive in 2025
notableInward2025: The Mummy (Lee Cronin; Atomic Monster/Blumhouse for New Line)

section481Spend2021.note: Previous record, per Screen Ireland's Section 481 data page

section481Credit.basis: 32% of the lowest of eligible expenditure, 80% of total qualifying production costs, or EUR 125m

scealUplift.condition: Independent feature films with qualifying expenditure up to EUR 20m globally (introduced Budget 2025)

vfxUplift.condition: Minimum EUR 1m eligible VFX expenditure; 40% on up to EUR 10m of eligible expenditure; subject to EU State Aid approval (Budget 2026)

qualifying.entryIntoInsurance: Must have started paying PRSI at least 10 years before drawing the pension (i.e. before age 56 to draw at 66)
qualifying.voluntary: High-rate voluntary contributions can make up the balance of the 520 if at least 260 full-rate employment contributions are paid

totalContributionsApproach.appliesTo: Anyone born on or after 1 January 1959 (claims from 1 January 2025)
counts: Full-rate paid contributions from employment (Class A) or self-employment (Class S)
HomeCaring Periods and Long-Term Carer's Contributions (may not overlap)
Up to 10 years (520) of credited contributions
totalContributionsApproach.creditsCap: Credited contributions capped at 10 years; HomeCaring Periods plus credits together capped at 1,040 (20 years)
totalContributionsApproach.contributionsCountedUntil: Age 66, or the age to which the pension is deferred

yearlyAveragePhaseOut.rule: From 2025 to 2034 a claimant gets the higher of pure TCA or a blend of Yearly Average (YA) and TCA; by 2034 only TCA (everyone born on or after 1 January 1968).

howClassesCount.classA: Employee PRSI; one contribution per week of insurable employment. Below EUR 352 a week the employee pays nothing but is still insured at Class A because the employer pays.
howClassesCount.classS: Self-employed PRSI; reckonable, full-rate for the State Pension (Contributory). Paid annually at 4.2% of total income (min EUR 650) from 1 Oct 2025.
howClassesCount.maxPerWeek: Only one contribution per contribution week (max 52 a year), whatever the mix of classes or credits
howClassesCount.classSWeeksNote: Not confirmed from a primary page how many weekly contributions a year of Class S is recorded as (commonly 52); see 'uncertain'.

creditsFromJobseekers.automatic: Credits are awarded automatically when not working, under 66, and getting Jobseeker's Benefit or Jobseeker's Pay-Related Benefit
creditsFromJobseekers.jobseekersAllowance: Not automatic on the means-tested Jobseeker's Allowance: requires paid or credited contributions in either of the last 2 tax years
creditsFromJobseekers.signingOnForCreditsOnly: Possible without a payment if paid/credited contributions in either of the last 2 tax years, and unemployed, available, capable and genuinely seeking work
creditsFromJobseekers.onePerWeek: Where part-time work and Jobseeker's Benefit fall in the same week, the paid contribution is awarded, not a credit
creditsFromJobseekers.pensionCap: Credits count toward the TCA only up to 10 years (520)

meansTest.taper: After the first EUR 30 of weekly means, the pension falls EUR 2.50 for every EUR 2.50 of means
meansTest.employmentDisregardNote: Up to EUR 200 a week from employment (not self-employment or farming) is disregarded, for the claimant and separately for a spouse/partner
meansTest.ownHome: Value of own home is not assessed
meansTest.roomRentalDisregard: Up to EUR 269.23 a week (EUR 14,000 a year) from renting a room in own home, under conditions

pendingBudget2027.status: Government reported (26 Sept 2026) to be considering a EUR 7.50 weekly increase for Budget 2027; no decision made. Would take non-contributory rates to 295.50 / 305.50.

taxCredits.note: Employee (PAYE) and Earned Income credits are alternatives: combined they cannot exceed EUR 2,000 for one person with both employment and self-employment income. The combined cap is established Revenue practice but was not re-confirmed in the 2026 summary; see 'uncertain'.

usc.exemptNote: If total income exceeds EUR 13,000, USC is paid on the full income
usc.changeFrom2025: 2% band ceiling raised from EUR 27,382 to EUR 28,700 from 1 January 2026
usc.reducedRate: Max 2% for those aged 70+, or full medical card holders under 70, with aggregate income of EUR 60,000 or less (continued for 2026 and 2027)

classS.sourceNote: Citizens Information states all PRSI rates rise by 0.15% on 1 Oct 2026; the explicit Class S figure is from a secondary source

classSDetail.base: Total income for tax purposes (gross less allowable expenses), or minimum payment, whichever is greater

uncertain: Irish Equity current rate cards (film, TV, theatre, audio, commercials) are behind the members' login at https://irishequity.ie/fees/; only the 2021 Irish Film Agreement schedule is publicly readable. Whether a successor to the 2021 film agreement has been signed is not publicly confirmed; its rollover clause keeps it in force until replaced.
No public per-episode TV rate, RTÉ drama rate, RTÉ radio drama rate or voice-over minimum was found: all null.
No current Irish Equity / Theatre Forum minimum weekly theatre rate was found. The EUR 381 figure is historical (old Irish Times article) and must not be used as current.
The EUR 850 daily actor buyout is a 2020 market rate card from a Swiss producers' survey, not a collective-agreement minimum.
Agency commission (10-15% typical, rarely over 20%) comes from secondary guides; no agency publishes its rate.
The age-80+ State Pension (Contributory) personal rate EUR 309.30 comes from Zurich Ireland, not a government page.
How many weekly contributions a year of Class S PRSI is recorded as for the TCA was not confirmed from a primary page.
The Employee/Earned Income credit combined cap of EUR 2,000 was not re-confirmed from a 2026 primary source.
The USC surcharge (additional 3%, i.e. 11%) on non-PAYE income over EUR 100,000 was not confirmed from a primary page in this pass; set to null.
Class S 4.35% from 1 October 2026 is stated explicitly only by secondary sources; Citizens Information says all PRSI rates rise 0.15% on that date.
Budget 2027 is due in October 2026 and may change pension rates, USC bands and credits from January 2027. A EUR 7.50 pension increase is under consideration (RTÉ, 26 Sept 2026).

Section 481 2025 spend (EUR 544m, +26%) is taken from Screen Daily's report of Screen Ireland's figures (29 Jan 2026); the Screen Ireland page itself was not retrieved, and no format breakdown or project count was obtained.
Teri Hayden's agency is named 'The Agency', not 'Teri Hayden Agency'; 'Lisa Richards' and 'The Lisa Richards Agency' are one agency.
